text:
IncidentBot: PAGING: p99 streaming tail latency > 2.0s in eu-west2 for service=streaming-gateway (alert: STREAM-TAIL-9012). Graphs: https://console.redwood/alerts/STREAM-TAIL-9012

alice_oncall: I'm looking. Frontend p95 is fine, p99 and tail spikes only on streaming routes to eu-west2. Lots of stalled frames reported.

bob-net: I see concurrent retransmit spikes on nat-gw-eu-west2-1, BQL shows +18% retransmits since 12:33UTC. Could be cross-AZ egress weirdness.

carol-sre: tagging in. Have we paged platform for failover? @dave-platform any quick switch to eu-west3 routing?

alice_oncall: @dave-platform requested. I'm running quick diagnostics now. Running tcpdump on gateway to confirm handshake spikes:
```
# tcpdump -ni eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0' -c 1000
12:33:41.123456 IP client -> nat-gw: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
12:33:41.223789 IP nat-gw -> client: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346
12:33:42.345678 IP client -> nat-gw: Retransmission, Flags [S]
```
Seems SYN retransmits and delayed SYN-ACKs.

bob-net: Also seeing DNS timeouts from gateway to resolver-1.eu: ~120ms -> 800ms spikes, NXDOMAINs not increased. TLS handshake times (ClientHello->ServerHello) median 50ms -> 900ms at tail.

dave-platform: Starting weighted routing to eu-west3 for streaming routes as a mitigation (canary 20% -> 50% if stable). Triggering via route switch: `/api/v1/routes/streaming?set=eu-west3-weight=20`

carol-sre: Good. Alice, can you temporarily disable prefix caching for affected sessions to reduce tail amplification while we shift routes? Runbook reference: https://runbooks/redwood/streaming-tail

alice_oncall: Prefetch/cache toggle set to off for route streaming-gateway-eu-west2. Noting: this may increase CPU but should reduce skewed cache misses.

eve-support: Support note: customers on dedicated capacity (AcmeCorp, NimbusGames) reported degraded live sessions at ~12:34UTC. No error codes in API, clients saw stalls and reconnects. Communicating to CS.

frank-cs: Notified AcmeCorp support channel. They're seeing players in single AZ drop out and reconnect to other regions. Asking for ETA and mitigation steps.

bob-net: Quick low-level findings: NAT ephemeral port use up to 92% on nat-gw-eu-west2-1, conntrack table at 85% of limit. Packet loss around 0.8% internal egress to mesh boundary, but retransmit rate causing effective stalls. Suspect NAT hairpinning + conntrack pressure during concurrent streaming session churn.

carol-sre: Mitigation checklist I'm executing: 
- failover-routing to eu-west3 (in progress)
- increase NAT gateway capacity (spin up nat-gw-eu-west2-2)
- bump conntrack and ephemeral port ranges on nat instances
- if persistent, consider blackholing problematic egress path and route via dedicated transit

alice_oncall: eu-west3 canary at 20% now. Monitoring tail latency on canary. p99 on canary 220ms. good signal. Moving to 50% per runbook.

dave-platform: Increased weights to 50%. Also provisioning nat-gw-eu-west2-2 (t2.large equivalent) — ETA ~3m.

bob-net: Pushed conntrack tune: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and ephemeral range `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='10240 65535'` on nat-gw-eu-west2-1. Observed immediate drop in conntrack pressure.

carol-sre: Good. After conntrack bump and route shift, p99 for streaming in eu-west2 dropped from ~2.4s to ~310ms within 40s. Tail stalls diminished.

alice_oncall: Recording customer impact: ~2.3% of streaming sessions saw a stall > 2s; focused on customers with high-AZ stickiness. No data loss, only reconnects and latency. Estimating 00:12 duration to full mitigation (start 12:33UTC -> 12:45UTC).

frank-cs: Updated AcmeCorp, NimbusGames with mitigation steps and ETA. They asked for postmortem and whether Dedicated capacity customers were affected differently.

eve-support: Dedicated customers on their own VPCs were less affected if they had private egress (bypassed NAT). Shared-hosting customers had heavier impact. Documenting in incident ticket INC-2026-3312.

carol-sre: Quick root cause hypothesis: NAT/conntrack saturation combined with intermittent cross-AZ egress packet loss (likely noisy host or intermediary routing device) produced SYN/TLS handshake amplification and streaming stalls at tail. The DNS timeouts amplified cold starts for some connections.

alice_oncall: Actions taken (short): 
- routing canary -> eu-west3 -> 50%
- increased nat capacity + conntrack/ephemeral ports
- disabled prefix caching on affected route briefly
- customer comms to impacted tenants

carol-sre: Next actions (post-incident): 
- run targeted gremlin on nat-gw-eu-west2-1 to reproduce and isolate host vs path
- add alert for conntrack_utilization >= 80% with auto-page
- add runbook step to prefer regional resolver pair on nat egress to avoid DNS tail effects
- evaluate sticky-AZ routing for streaming flows to reduce hairpinning

dave-platform: I'll follow up with infra to size NAT fleet and add autoscaling trigger for ephemeral port usage.

alice_oncall: Handoff to @carol-sre for postmortem. I'm back to next rotation. Paging clear from my side. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged by carol-sre. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket: INC-2026-3312.

carol-sre: I'll take it from here, will kick off postmortem and include timeline, metrics, and recommended long-term fixes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
